sentence: This project studies the different isoforms of a protein that hair cells need for hearing and how they are controlled.
This project tests whether aging T lymphocytes make an inflammatory molecule that disrupts lymphatic vessels of the brain in Alzheimer's disease.
This project combines classical epidemiology, genomic epidemiology, clinical investigations and laboratory studies to study the causes and outcomes of childhood cancer.
This project studies how alcohol plays a role in sexual violence among pairs of Marine men who drink together.
This project provides services from library preparation to basic data analysis, focused mainly on next-generation sequencing.
This project tries to find the circuits, molecules and cell types that form and change emotional social memories.
This project builds a center that supports studies of the mechanisms driving or restraining early cancers.
This project finds genetic variations that contribute to risks for multiple pediatric cancer types and builds tools to predict who may develop them.
This project builds imaging tools for live cells and tissue to find the physical barriers that limit the immune response against tumors.
This project tries to find the factors and signaling pathways that control a chanzyme in mouse oocytes and cleaving embryos.
This project studies how inflammatory cytokine signaling pathways and cell intrinsic and extrinsic mechanisms drive clonal expansion in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
This project studies how air pollution, social isolation and rural built environments affect cognitive function in farmworkers at risk for Alzheimer's disease.
This project uses Positron Emission Tomography imaging to track where phages go and build up in rats with cystic fibrosis.
This project uses specialized cameras and 3D scanners to look at how new blood vessels form in the hands of scleroderma patients.
This project makes viral and nonviral constructs that deliver genes and proteins into cells and skin.
This project develops polymeric micelles that carry an imaging agent through the nose to brain tumor tissue and give a fluorescence signal there.
This project tests whether one major driver behind triple negative breast cancer aggressiveness also explains racial disparities in this disease.
This project studies the circuit and cellular mechanisms by which stress undermines extinction learning.
This project uses emerging techniques to match current medications to cystic fibrosis mutations and find the optimal drug combination for each patient.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms of male and female interplay that lead to reproductive success in flowering plants.
